head: claude/mi-162-document-index-population
title: MI-162 — fix the document-index POPULATION (971 → 999) and add the control that was missing
body:
## The finding

`scripts/ops/document_index.py::POPULATION_GLOBS` contained `docs/**/*.md`, which is handed to `git ls-files` as a **pathspec**, not to Python's `glob`. In a pathspec with no magic, git matches with wildmatch **without** `WM_PATHNAME`: `*` already crosses `/` (so bare `docs/*.md` is recursive) while `docs/**/` requires a **literal** intervening slash. Every `.md` sitting directly in `docs/` was therefore outside the population.

Verified with `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`:

| pathspec | files | top-level | nested |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/**/*.md` | 936 | **0** | 936 |
| `:(glob)docs/**/*.md` | 964 | **28** | 936 |

**Population 971 → 999.** The 28 include the two documents that *outrank* `CLAUDE.md` — `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` (instruction hierarchy level 1) and `docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md` (level 2) — plus `docs/api-tier-policy.md`, `docs/SPRINT-LOG-TEMPLATE-CANONICAL.md`, `docs/TRADE-PIPELINE.md` and `docs/workplan.md`.

Meanwhile the guard printed `population=971 registered=971` / `document-index: OK`. **100% coverage of a population that silently excluded its most important members** — UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class C (an unasserted denominator), and the **second** instance of that class in this one function: `population()`'s own docstring records the first (`--others --exclude-standard` missing, *"reported OK and the count never moved"*).

## Why `:(glob)` and not bare `docs/*.md`

Both yield 964. `docs/*.md` works *only* because `*` crosses `/` — the very non-obvious behaviour that caused this bug — so it would leave the next reader in the same trap. `:(glob)` selects wildmatch **with** `WM_PATHNAME`, under which `/**/` means "zero or more directories", and the pattern finally means what every reader already thought it meant. `.claude/skills/**/*.md` carried the identical latent defect (every skill is nested one deep today, so it excluded nothing) and is fixed the same way rather than left to bite later.

## The control that was missing

`--self-test` fed known-bad input to the **rule engine**, which was never the defect: `evaluate()` is a pure function over a population it is *handed*, so a population filtered before it runs is invisible to it by construction. All 13 rule cases pass throughout the bug.

So the self-test now also runs `population_control()`, which plants **real files** — a top-level `docs/*.md`, a nested `docs/claude/*.md`, and a `docs/*.txt` that must **not** appear — and asserts `population()` sees exactly the right ones.

**Verified it catches this bug**: re-run against the old pathspec, 13/13 rule cases PASS and the population control is the *only* failure, naming the pathspec as the cause. A control that cannot plant its files FAILS rather than skipping. A fix that hand-added 28 rows while leaving the glob intact would not have satisfied it.

## Status of the 28 new rows — counted, not asserted

**4 carry an established status; 24 read `unknown`.**

| status | n | basis |
|---|---|---|
| `live` | 3 | `ci:canonical-doc-coherence-ACTIVE_DOCS` |
| `historical` | 1 | `mi159:plan-status-header` (`docs/workplan.md`) |
| `unknown` | 24 | `not-assessed` |

`unknown` means *we did not look*, and for 24 documents nobody has read it is the correct value. No status was manufactured to improve the census (551 → 574 unknown, on a population 28 larger).

## Two registers, now agreeing

`docs/workplan.md` was graded `historical` by `scripts/ci/check_one_live_workplan.py` — **in** that guard's population — while being invisible to the document index: 1 of MI-159's 13 plan documents outside the register. **All 13 are now registered and the two populations agree** (`set(mi159) - population()` is empty).

## `TASK-PRIORITY-2026-09-07.md`

Shipped stamped `unknown · last verified never · nobody has verified this document's status`, because it was written minutes before the index landed. Read in full here and given a true header (`live` / `plan`) via a new `STATUS_EXPLICIT` map — consulted **last**, below every imported, CI-enforced, structural and self-declared rule, so it can only ever convert `unknown` into a recorded determination and never overrule a machine-checkable one. It holds exactly one entry, deliberately; its comment forbids bulk-adding entries to drain the `unknown` column.

## Also in this PR

Two `docs/*.md` files revealed by the fix are **generated** wholesale by their own `--matrix` generator, so a stamp written into them is erased on the next run and their guards fail with *"matrix is stale"* — observed on this branch's first full guard run, not predicted. They join `GENERATED` (waiver verified at build time), staying registered with only the R3 header rule waived. `generated_waived` 2 → 4.

## The backlog row this dispatch cited did not exist

The dispatch stated the finding was already *"filed as `BL-20260907-DOCUMENT-INDEX-POPULATION-GLOB-EXCLUDES-EVERY-TOP-LEVEL-DOCS-FILE`"*. It was not: `grep` returned **0** across all four backlogs, with a positive control (a known row id in the same file returns 1) proving the probe was live. Filed here from this session's own measurement, along with a recurrence row — this is the third *"the dispatch names a durable artifact that does not exist"* in the same workstream in two days (MI-148, MI-156, MI-162), and the existing sibling row's resolution criteria are scoped to work-object *paths*, so satisfying them as written would not catch a cited backlog id.

## Verification

- `scripts/ci/check_document_index.py` → `population=999 registered=999 headers_read=999 generated_waived=4` · `OK`
- `scripts/ci/check_document_index.py --self-test` → 13 rule cases + 3 planted files, all pass
- `scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py --base origin/main` → `state=declared_self_land`
- `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` → **PASS 70 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 20**

Tier 1 (docs, CI, tooling). No runtime, no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps, no service or timer, no live-VM file.
